claims.text: Applying a boron nitride coating to steel components used in hot dip aluminum plating significantly reduces corrosion by molten aluminum.
Conventional tool steel is typically used for rollers and guide plates in hot dip aluminum plating equipment.
A uniform, high-quality boron nitride coating should be deposited onto the steel components.
The intended operating condition is prolonged immersion in high-temperature molten aluminum during industrial hot dip plating.
The BN coating forms a barrier that isolates the steel substrate from direct contact with molten aluminum.
BN has low wettability toward molten aluminum.
BN is chemically inert and has low reactivity with aluminum under the stated operating conditions.
The BN layer minimizes chemical interaction between molten aluminum and the underlying steel.
The BN layer minimizes adhesion of molten aluminum to the underlying component.
Reduced chemical interaction and adhesion decrease corrosion and erosion of the steel component.
BN-coated components will have significantly lower corrosion rates than uncoated steel components.
BN-coated components will have longer service lives than uncoated steel components.
The beneficial effect depends on the BN coating retaining its integrity at high temperature and during prolonged thermal cycling.
Coating adhesion and resistance to thermal and mechanical stresses are critical to performance.
Laboratory-scale tests support the corrosion resistance of boron nitride in high-temperature environments.
Long-term performance of BN coatings under industrial-scale aluminum plating conditions has not been fully validated.
